Predict the biomass of in situ surveys

Source: R/kb_predict_biomass_in_situ.R
kb_predict_biomass_in_situ.Rd

Combine a weight fit with the plants counted by each in situ survey into the biomass of the surveyed area: wet or dry (kg/m² or kg), or carbon or nitrogen (g/m² or kg).

Usage

kb_predict_biomass_in_situ(
  weight,
  size,
  survey,
  wetdry = NULL,
  carbon = NULL,
  nitrogen = NULL,
  ...,
  measure = c("wet", "dry", "carbon", "nitrogen"),
  per_area = TRUE,
  pool_by = NULL,
  new_levels = c("sample", "average"),
  representative_site = NULL,
  n_plants = 100L,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  estimate = stats::median,
  sig_fig = 3,
  progress = c("bar", "none"),
  progress_dir = NULL
)

Arguments

weight

A kb_fit_weight object.

size

A kb_fit_size object, or a size census, a data frame with one row per counted plant (see kb_check_data_size_census_nereo() and kb_check_data_size_census_macro() for the columns).

survey

A data frame of in situ surveys, one row per survey (see kb_check_data_survey_in_situ() for the columns).

wetdry

A kb_fit_wetdry object, required for dry, carbon, and nitrogen biomass, or NULL. All fits must be of the same species and have the same number of draws.

carbon

A kb_fit_carbon object, required for carbon biomass, or NULL.

nitrogen

A kb_fit_nitrogen object, required for nitrogen biomass, or NULL.

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

measure

A string, one of "wet", "dry", "carbon", or "nitrogen", giving the type of biomass to predict.

per_area

A flag specifying whether to give biomass per m² of the surveyed area, or else the biomass in that area.

pool_by

A character vector naming character or factor columns to group the rows by, such as c("site", "year"), character(0) to pool all rows, or NULL (the default) for one row per input row. On each draw, the biomass of a group is the sum of its rows' biomass (kg). For another summary, such as an unweighted mean of rows, summarise the draws column, for example with posterior::rvar_mean().

new_levels

A string giving how uncertainty is shown for a site or year not in the fit. Sites and years in the fit always use their own estimates. One of:

  • "sample" (the default): a new effect for each new site or year, drawn from the estimated variation among sites or among years (the random-effect standard deviation). The point estimate is equivalent, but the interval is wider since it also includes that variation. Use it to get realistic uncertainty about a particular site or year that the model has no information on. The interval varies slightly between calls; use set.seed() to reproduce it.

  • "average": the typical site or year. The site and year effects are set to 0, their mean, so the interval does not include among-site or among-year variation. Use it to describe an average site or year.

representative_site

A character vector of sites whose effects a new site takes in every fit (averaged when several are named), a list naming the sites per fit, such as list(weight = "site_a"), where a fit left out follows new_levels, or NULL (the default) to follow new_levels.

n_plants

A whole number of sizes averaged per draw to compute the mean plant weight from a size fit; larger values are more precise and slower. Not used with a size census.

conf_level

A number greater than 0 and less than 1 giving the compatibility-interval level.

estimate

A function that reduces a numeric vector of posterior draws to a single estimate, such as median or mean.

sig_fig

A whole number of significant figures for summary output.

progress

A string, one of "bar" (the default, a console progress bar) or "none" (silent).

progress_dir

A string giving an existing directory in which to record progress for kb_progress(), or NULL (the default) to record none.

Value

A kb_predictions object: the rows of survey, or one row per pool_by group, with weight_support and, with a size fit, size_support (as in kb_predict_mean_weight()), the draws of the biomass (for example biomass_kg_m2 or carbon_biomass_kg), and estimate, lower, and upper.

Details

Plant sizes come from a size fit, when only a sample of plants was measured, or from a size census, when every counted plant was measured, joined to its survey by survey_id (see Methods). A survey with no rows in the size census has zero biomass, and a message lists such surveys. With pool_by and per_area = TRUE, a group's biomass per m² is its summed biomass over its summed survey_area_m2.

See also

kb_fit_cover_calibration_nereo() to calibrate plot cover on the result.

Other prediction functions: autoplot.kb_predictions(), kb_new_data(), kb_plot_predictions(), kb_predict_biomass_canopy(), kb_predict_carbon(), kb_predict_cover_calibration(), kb_predict_mean_weight(), kb_predict_nitrogen(), kb_predict_size(), kb_predict_weight(), kb_predict_wetdry(), predict.kb_fit_carbon(), predict.kb_fit_cover_calibration(), predict.kb_fit_nitrogen(), predict.kb_fit_size(), predict.kb_fit_weight(), predict.kb_fit_wetdry()

Examples

# Tallied plants, sizes from a size fit
set.seed(1)
kb_predict_biomass_in_situ(
  fit_weight_sim_nereo,
  fit_size_sim_nereo,
  data_survey_in_situ_sim_nereo
)
#> <kb_predictions> response: biomass_kg_m2 | by: site, year
#> # A tibble: 54 × 14
#>    survey_id       site  year  survey_area_m2 plants plot_area_m2 canopy_area_m2
#>    <chr>           <fct> <fct>          <dbl>  <int>        <dbl>          <dbl>
#>  1 otter_cove-202… otte… 2020            140     992         215            87.3
#>  2 otter_cove-202… otte… 2020             80     297         262.          110. 
#>  3 gull_rock-2020… gull… 2020            233.    660         233.           30.3
#>  4 cedar_bay-2020… ceda… 2020             40       0         270.           34.3
#>  5 cedar_bay-2020… ceda… 2020            180     861         255.           81.2
#>  6 heron_reef-202… hero… 2020            120     550         217.           73.5
#>  7 urchin_shoal-2… urch… 2020            160    1815         218.          116. 
#>  8 sculpin_head-2… scul… 2020            193.   1245         193.           30.1
#>  9 eagle_spit-202… eagl… 2020            200     471         259.           97.3
#> 10 tidepool_bluff… tide… 2020            180     698         229            62.3
#> # ℹ 44 more rows
#> # ℹ 7 more variables: canopy_tide_height_m <dbl>, weight_support <chr>,
#> #   size_support <chr>, biomass_kg_m2 <rvar[1d]>, estimate <dbl>, lower <dbl>,
#> #   upper <dbl>

# A site the weight fit has no data for, weighed like a fitted site
set.seed(1)
kb_predict_biomass_in_situ(
  fit_weight_sim_nereo,
  fit_size_sim_nereo,
  subset(data_survey_in_situ_sim_nereo, site == "fog_islet"),
  representative_site = list(weight = "otter_cove")
)
#> <kb_predictions> response: biomass_kg_m2 | by: site, year
#> # A tibble: 4 × 14
#>   survey_id        site  year  survey_area_m2 plants plot_area_m2 canopy_area_m2
#>   <chr>            <fct> <fct>          <dbl>  <int>        <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 fog_islet-2021-1 fog_… 2021            207.    278         207.          122. 
#> 2 fog_islet-2022-1 fog_… 2022            217.    346         217.          108. 
#> 3 fog_islet-2024-1 fog_… 2024            218.    253         218.           50.5
#> 4 fog_islet-2025-1 fog_… 2025            229.    423         229.           84.3

#> #   size_support <chr>, biomass_kg_m2 <rvar[1d]>, estimate <dbl>, lower <dbl>,
#> #   upper <dbl>

# Every counted plant measured
set.seed(1)
kb_predict_biomass_in_situ(
  fit_weight_sim_macro,
  data_size_census_sim_macro,
  data_survey_in_situ_sim_macro,
  pool_by = c("site", "year")
)
